svg.title: STAFF ENGINEER CHEAT SHEET: sketchnote
svg.text: Frame the tension · say the number · decide and own the
trade-off · raise failures first · run it · evolve it.
A senior answer gets a working design. A staff answer explains why this design, what it costs, how it fails, and how it will be run.
Clarifies the goal, cuts scope on purpose
One decisive number rules options in or
Chooses, says what is given up and when
CP or AP per feature, with the cost
Prices the expensive part, designs around
What breaks at 10×; simple today on
Drives the agenda, checks in, invites
Timeouts with unknown outcome → idempotency keys, reconcile
Hot keys and celebrity users → split keys, hybrid fan-out
Cache stampede → single-flight, jittered TTLs, serve stale
Replica lag → read-your-writes where it matters
Leader or node failure → failover time, data loss window, fencing
Thundering herds → backoff with jitter, admission control, waiting rooms
Abuse and bots → rate limits, signed tokens
One SLO per critical path (p99 latency,
Pipeline health: queue depth, consumer lag,
Roll out behind flags; shadow mode for risky
Rollback plan for every schema or config
Reconciliation jobs where money or inventory

"This path is CP, that one is AP, because…"
"I'd watch A and B, and alert on C."
"At 10× the first thing to break is…, so I'd…"

Every new system adds on-call load
